prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-22. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 1.18 |
| Retained earnings       | 17,162M |
| Current liabilities     | 105,547M |
| Current assets          | 124,141M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 5,987M |
| Total liabilities       | 158,800M |
| Total assets            | 164,787M |
| EBIT / operating income | 446M |
| Revenue                 | 22,217M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-22, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported balance sheet shows extreme leverage (equity is only ~3.6% of assets and total liabilities nearly equal total assets) together with thin liquidity (current ratio 1.18) and very low operating profitability (EBIT margin ~2%). These metrics place the firm deep in the speculative-grade range and are consistent with material default risk, though not yet an outright payment default.
DECISION: CCC
(The final rating reflects only the static ratios supplied and pre-2026 rating conventions; no forward-looking adjustments are possible from the given data.)
